subject: Inference scoping — recommended models & verified perf profiles
messages:
From: Clara Huang <clara@novusai.com>

Cc: procurement@novusai.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from scoping call — Novus AI inference goals

Thanks again for the call this morning, Diego — good to meet you and Marissa. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned before you send recommended models and perf artifacts: 

- Primary goal: real-time summarization + entity extraction for live support transcripts (customer volume ~200 concurrent sessions during peak).
- Hard SLO: p99 latency <= 200ms on the inference layer for user-facing requests (we accept slightly higher for heavy-context bookkeeping).
- Target throughput: ~1,200 reqs/minute sustained, spikes to ~2,500 for 3–5 minute windows.
- Quality baseline: current internal model achieves 88% exact-entity recall on our eval corpus; we need parity or better.
- Compliance: data residency in US only and SOC2 evidence required for pilot.

Action items for Redwood: please share the shortlist of models you recommend for pilot, Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles), and any prompt sets you suggest for regression checks. Also send any drive links or dashboards we can review.

Thanks — Clara
Clara Huang
Head of AI Platform, Novus AI
clara@novusai.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Hi Clara — great to meet you. Below is a concise pilot recommendation set plus links to Redwood-verified performance profiles and a prompt pack for your regression checks. I summarized TPS and latency percentiles for the model variants we think are closest to your risk/latency envelope.

Shortlist (recommended order for pilot):
1) redwood-reasoner-7b-q4_1 (quantized) — best cost/latency balance for short summarization prompts; strong throughput.
2) redwood-reasoner-13b-8k (fp16) — higher quality for long-context support transcripts; expect higher p99 but better entity recall.
3) open-llm-13b-qlora (compat) — fallback when we need extra semantic fidelity; slightly higher token costs.

Redwood-verified perf snapshot (see attached CSV and drive dashboard link):
- redwood-reasoner-7b-q4_1: median latency (p50) = 28ms, p95 = 86ms, p99 = 160ms at 1000 TPS (configured batch window = 12ms); sustained TPS up to 3,200 with continuous batching on a 4x A100 pool.
- redwood-reasoner-13b-8k: p50 = 55ms, p95 = 170ms, p99 = 260ms at 600 TPS; recommend reserved capacity for predictable p99 under your spike profile.
- open-llm-13b-qlora: p50 = 42ms, p95 = 120ms, p99 = 220ms at 800 TPS.

Notes on SLOs and tradeoffs:
- For p99 <= 200ms across your peak profile I recommend piloting redwood-reasoner-7b-q4_1 as the primary engine for user-facing summarization, with 13b-8k as a canary/passive-compare variant for quality checks. That combination keeps cost down while giving you a quality baseline.
- Continuous KV caching for session state (we saw 30–45% token savings on similar workloads) will materially improve p99 for repeated context.

Prompt/Regression pack: attached 'novus_pilot_promptpack_v1.txt' contains:
- 35 targeted prompts covering short/long context, adversarial entity masking, and hallucination probes.
- Expected gold labels and a simple scoring rubric (precision/recall for entity extraction, ROUGE-L for summarization).

Attachments (stubs): redwood_verified_profiles_aug2026.csv (perf snapshots), novus_pilot_promptpack_v1.txt (prompt/test set), MAP_NovusAI_20260816.pdf (mutual action plan).

Links:
- Drive perf dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBz-example-benchmarks
- Benchmark dashboard (live): https://redwood.example.com/bench-dashboard/novusai-7792
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7792

Next steps I propose:
- You share the eval corpus (1–2 representative days of transcripts) and we run the first 72-hour side-by-side on hosted Redwood infra.
- Kickoff call for pilot setup (60 minutes) this week — we can do Wed/Fri morning PT.
- Mutual action plan + procurement step (DocuSign link in MAP).

Marissa (copied) will follow up with an exact perf runbook and the intake checklist for your security team (SOC2 artifacts).

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Clara — adding a few concrete numbers and an internal runbook pointer to the items Diego sent.

Concrete perf context (full-run caveats apply):
- Our public perf snapshots are measured with Redwood continuous-batching enabled and a 12ms batching window unless otherwise noted. The CSV Diego attached includes raw traces (p10/p25/p50/p75/p95/p99) per model and per sequence-length bucket.
- For a 2,500-rpm spike profile we recommend a Dedicated Reservation with autoscale headroom (policy: target CPU/GPU util 65–80%). That avoids p99 tail amplification during bursts.

Quality/regression checklist we will run during the 72-hour side-by-side:
- Baseline metric comparisons (entity recall/precision, summary ROUGE-L).
- Adversarial prompt set from novus_pilot_promptpack_v1.txt (we'll run these hourly to detect regressions).
- Canary routing: implement passive-compare routing to 13b-8k variant for 10% of traffic for the first week.

Security artifacts: Diego will share the SOC2 summary and audit contact; procurement, please expect an email with a short security questionnaire and a link to the compliance pack repo.

I'll drop a short runbook in the Drive folder and create a Jira ticket for the pilot onboarding work: SUP-4321 (intake -> infra -> test -> go/no-go).

Action items assigned: 
- Novus: send eval corpus + confirm pilot start window (Clara).
- Redwood (Marissa): create SUP-4321 and populate runbook + attach SOC2 summary (ETA EOD tomorrow).
- Redwood (Diego): share final MAP + perf CSV (done).
